overview: Tooth extraction is the process of removing a damaged, decayed, or problematic tooth from its socket in the jawbone. It is typically performed when the tooth cannot be saved through other treatments such as fillings, crowns, or root canals.
overviewImageAlt: Forceps extracting a tooth from the jawbone
reasons: Severe tooth decay or damage beyond repair
Impacted wisdom teeth causing pain or crowding
Gum disease leading to loose teeth
Infection or abscess that cannot be treated with antibiotics

procedure.title: Diagnosis
procedure.description: We examine your teeth and take X-rays to assess the condition of the tooth and surrounding structures.

procedure.title: Anesthesia
procedure.description: Local anesthesia is applied to numb the area and ensure your comfort.

procedure.title: Extraction
procedure.description: For simple extractions, the tooth is gently loosened and removed. For surgical extractions, a small incision is made in the gum to remove the tooth.

procedure.title: Post-Procedure Care
procedure.description: The area is cleaned, and stitches may be placed if necessary. Post-extraction instructions are provided to aid healing.

whyChooseUs: Focus on patient comfort and care
Transparent pricing and flexible appointment scheduling

faqs.question: Is tooth extraction painful?
faqs.answer: No, local anesthesia ensures the procedure is painless. You may feel slight pressure but no pain.

faqs.question: How long does it take to recover?
faqs.answer: Most patients recover within 7 to 10 days. Following post-care instructions can speed up the healing process.

faqs.question: Can I go to work after extraction?
faqs.answer: It is advisable to rest for at least 24 hours after the procedure. For surgical extractions, you may need 2 to 3 days of rest.

faqs.question: What happens if I don't extract an infected tooth?
faqs.answer: Ignoring an infected tooth can lead to severe pain, swelling, and the spread of infection to other parts of your body.

faqs.question: Are there alternatives?
faqs.answer: If the tooth can be saved, treatments like root canal therapy or dental crowns may be recommended.
